observation.description: guide/clients/react-expo.md is the sanctioned page for this arm's exact task, and its only hook snippet shows a checkpoint-era object form - useSnapbackQuery({ provider, query, userId, authority }) - that does not exist on packaged 0.1.7 (the shipped hook is useSnapbackQuery(ref, args) under a SnapbackProvider, per clients/react.md), and whose userId field teaches dev-mode client-asserted identity. The page also directs RN consumers to bindSnapbackAppLifecycle(AppState, liveHandle) 'when a provider exposes the first-party liveQuery handle' - the documented React provider path never exposes such a handle, so the helper is unreachable from the path the same page prescribes. Nothing on the page mentions the WebCrypto prerequisite (f1), the in-memory store consequence (f3), or how the Online nonclaim interacts with the offlineQueue option (f2).

competitorOutcome.description: Firebase and Expo both ship RN quickstarts that compile against the shipped SDK surface; provider docs teaching a nonexistent call shape is below any current bar.

mustNotRegress: The page's honest evidence-boundary framing (per-OS receipts, no physical-device claim, anti-pattern list).
smallestCoherentFix: Rewrite the page against the packaged 0.1.7 surface (context provider + (ref, args) hook, external-bearer session boot, crypto prerequisite, store/queue nonclaims with their mechanics) with CI-verified snippets, and either expose a lifecycle seam on the React provider or drop the unreachable helper reference.
acceptanceWitness: node scripts/check-guide.mjs compiles the page's snippets against the packaged closure, and a fresh agent following only this page reaches a live query on an Expo simulator.
